(1) the use of spatial features (i.e. i, j, and k coordinates) in conjunction with intensity features improves the performance of the classification methods, (2) the use of a Gaussian kernel in conjunction with the spatial features improves the performance further, and (3) the performance of the method is further improved by adapting the hyper-parameters for each brain.

(1) within-brain classification for segmentation can be more accurate than between-brain classification; (2) the addition of spatial features to intensity features significantly improves classification performance; (3) the use of a kernel that is more appropriate for MRI data improves the performance of classification methods; (4) the use of an adaptive hyper-parameter selection method can further improve performance.
